WIC17A-01.note: Layer is ground off and binned unanalyzed, so the step sacrifices material. 'Diagnostic' tempts (first step of an analysis) but the powder is explicitly not analyzed; 'redundant' fails because the layer is the richest, not superfluous.

WIC17A-02.note: She suspects the effect depends on the new anesthetic protocol: contingent. 'Spurious' is the main pull but the placebo arm rules out a fluke and she believes the effect is real; 'marginal' is refuted by 'a large effect'.

WIC17A-03.note: Final sentence (parts swapped by two workers in an afternoon) alone gives repairable. 'Durable' tempts but repeated replacements cut against it; affordable and substantial are each refuted by a planted clause (cost more; strength unknown).

WIC17A-04.note: Bees visit constantly but contribute no seed: pollinators in name only, nominal. 'Occasional' fails because they are the most frequent visitor; 'exclusive' and 'efficient' are refuted by the bumblebee and bagging evidence. Hard mainly because of the less common sense of 'nominal'.

WIC17A-05.note: 'Where they are present, it simply reports nothing' decides silent. 'Fickle' is the designed trap and is killed by 'behaves the same way on every scan'; sluggish (within seconds) and invasive (no flake removed) are each refuted by a planted clause.

WIC17A-06.note: Two halves of different ages separated by a buried soil make the arc composite. 'Fragmentary' tempts (two pieces) but the arc is unbroken and complete; 'displaced' is refuted by the last sentence, 'uniform' by the dating.

WIC17B-01.note: Reports cover only cases judges chose to circulate, so the figure is partial (incomplete and skewed). 'Inexact' is the strongest pull, but the count is a complete tally of reported decisions, so it is precise about what it covers; 'trivial' is refuted by 'still worth knowing'.

WIC17B-02.note: Showing a drawing instead of naming the object elicits the word indirectly, avoiding the order effect in the pilot. Hurried (waited a full minute) and public (alone with a fieldworker) are refuted by planted clauses; 'voluntary' is the only real pull, but nothing concerns the speaker's choice to participate. Note that 'neutral' would fit better than the key.

WIC17B-03.note: On the books but unenforced: prices did not move, open smuggling, no petitions, so nominal. Temporary (kept to 1831), ruinous (prices did not move), and disputed (never petitioned) are each refuted by a dedicated clause.

WIC17B-04.note: The plain tune is 'no longer the tune', so the ornaments are integral. Optional is the transcribers' view the passage overturns; individual (every fiddler placed them alike) and borrowed (found in no neighboring repertory) are each refuted by a planted sentence.

WIC17B-05.note: The same castle is reused behind three saints from one pattern drawing, so the landscapes are generic. Unfinished (fully painted), specified (contracts never mention setting), and symbolic (no bearing on the legends) each get one dedicated refuting clause.

WIC17B-06.note: Equal payments and one payout per member per cycle make the arrangement reciprocal. Charitable is the received view that 'suggest otherwise' overturns; compulsory (members could leave) and secretive (read aloud) are refuted by planted clauses.
